title: Oral Hygiene Performed by Dental Laypersons on a Phantom Model: Cleaner-Centered Analysis, Development, and Evaluation of an Educational Intervention on Oral Health for People in Need of Care (FRAIL) FRAIL: Oral hygiene performed by relatives; intervention; layperson.
summary:
The main objective of this clinical study is to investigate whether personalized training based on initial toothbrushing behavior improves the effectiveness of oral hygiene performed by laypeople, as measured by dental plaque (also known as biofilm), using phantom models.


This study is a single-center, prospective, randomized controlled trial (RCT). The toothbrushing process is simulated using plastic models.
Study participants are randomly divided into two groups. Each group has two study appointments.
All participants perform a brushing procedure on the plastic models. This simulates brushing for people in need of care as it would be performed in the context of supportive oral care. A video recording is made of the brushing process. 
Then, participants in Group 1 (the case group) receive personalized group training on oral care for individuals in need of care based on their respective brushing process. The training covers different situations, ergonomics, aids, and the oral care process. 
Participants in Group 2 (the control group) will receive training materials and access to an online training platform on home oral care. This corresponds to the standard procedure.
 
At a follow-up appointment, approximately one to two weeks after the initial appointment, all participants are asked to demonstrate the cleaning procedure on plastic models again. Then, they are asked to answer questions about their subjective assessment of oral care for people in need of care.
 
At a third appointment, two months after the training, all participants will be asked again to perform the cleaning procedure on plastic models to check long-term success.
The results of the study will help analyze third-party cleaning behavior and provide information on the effectiveness of individualized oral care training.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Interest and consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
• Completed, discontinued, or ongoing vocational training in dentistry (e.g., dentist, dental assistant, dental hygienist, or dental prophylaxis assistant).
 
• Completed, discontinued, or ongoing nursing training (e.g., geriatric care, health and (pediatric) nursing, or nursing specialist).
• Other completed, discontinued, or ongoing medical or therapeutic specialist training that includes a professional qualification in nursing or dentistry.
• Insufficient knowledge of German
• Physical or cognitive impairment affecting the ability to clean teeth
• Lack of written consent
